body:
D1 / D5 / D6 DISPOSITION: AMEND. The advisor has the right semantic direction, but the proposed stack needs a stricter authority gradient and a smaller first slice. In particular, a generic provider layer or unified observation supertype now would fuse three things that this repository deliberately keeps separate: source evidence, sidecar measurement, and proposal authority.

D1 — ACQUISITION BOUNDARY AND MODULE OWNERSHIP

ACCEPT the ADR 0007 ownership split as the controlling design:

- `core` owns medium-neutral source identity and evidence geometry: `SourceBundle`, nonempty `EvidenceSupport`, path-dependent `PresentationAxis`, and checked `NarrativeSourceAtlas`. It remains portable and cats-only.
- `features` owns aligned scalar/vector/categorical observations and derivations. An embedding or detector output stays a feature sidecar; it never becomes identity, graph structure, or evidence merely because it is accurate.
- `acquire` owns bounded task packets, proposal/alternative/abstention outcomes, critic findings, and the deterministic resolution transition. Only the resolver creates `Accepted`.
- `story` and `document` consume resolved claims and validated source support. They do not import provider APIs.
- decoder, media I/O, model runtimes, Python/RPC, HTTP, and GPU code live in a separately authorized JVM adapter after Q5 and dependency review. No reverse dependency from a portable module is permitted.

AMEND the advisor by rejecting a portable `Observation` umbrella and by not promoting embedding-specific contracts into generic worker authority. `embed-core` supplies good patterns — policy-minted authorization, per-item `BatchResult`, fail-closed receipts, sidecar identity — but `AuthorizedRemoteRequest` and embedding geometry are intentionally domain-specific. Reuse the construction pattern, not those semantic types.

The smallest coherent implementation slice I would authorize first is Stage C1, before any provider:

1. `core`: smart-constructed bundle, stream, axis, coordinate/interval, nonempty interval-set, support, and checked source-atlas contracts; a text conformance adapter must express the present `StorySource` and `SurfaceAtlas` without changing their semantics.
2. `laws`: construction-boundary courts plus bundle membership, axis identity, no-mixed-hull, missingness, boundary-layer distinction, and deterministic fingerprint laws.
3. `codec` is an immediate follower only after the constructors and wire discriminators settle; it must not force a premature all-module migration.

That is the smallest slice with an honest domain and refusal behavior. Do not include a model worker, FeatureTarget expansion, StoryModel envelope migration, or source-breaking resolver change in the same candidate. Stage C2 can then migrate evidence consumers; the JVM adapter is a later bead gated by exact source admission.

Current-source collisions that make this sequencing load-bearing:

- `core.Evidence` carries only `Option[SpanSet]`, and `ClaimMeta.spanLaw` defines `SurfaceExplicit` by span presence. A film interval cannot be stuffed into this without silently weakening evidence-first semantics. The successor must test eligible support by claim family, not accept any nonempty anchor.
- `acquire.Resolver.hasSpans` and `FamilyPolicy.requireSpanEvidence` are text-only. They need an evidence-eligibility policy over typed anchors while retaining the rule that only the resolver accepts.
- `TaskReferences.validateAgainst` is pinned to `SurfaceAtlas`, sentence/token IDs, and string node IDs. `TaskKind.Custom` is not permission to encode core film semantics as strings.
- `FeatureTarget` is a closed, ordered, persisted text/narrative domain. Media intervals cannot be normalized into `Window` or smuggled through labels; appending media cases changes rank/address codecs and needs an explicit migration.
- `FeatureObservation.support`, `SupportResolver`, and `FeatureTrack.restrict` all use `SpanSet`. Their successor must preserve axis identity and atlas membership, not just numeric overlap.
- `FeatureTrack` is a public case class even though its Scaladoc says its invariants are checked by `validated`; callers can construct an unsorted or duplicate track directly. A media worker must never be allowed to return a value whose static type falsely implies those invariants. Before media extension, close that construction boundary or distinguish draft from validated tracks.
- `ProviderCall` binds provider/model/version, input/output checksums, params, seed, and cache flag, but it does not independently type model weights, container/runtime, preprocessing, output schema, artifact coverage, or bundle/stream/axis identity. Encoding all of those into `params: Map[String,String]` would be stringly authority.
- resolver agreement currently keys only `(provider, model, version)`. That is too weak to treat different weight/config/preprocessing identities as independent reproducible evidence.
- `BuildReceipt` and `TrackProvenance` assume one story checksum. A bundle with multiple streams needs a bundle fingerprint plus exact stream/axis/extent bindings.

D5 — OBSERVATION TO CHART BOUNDARY

ACCEPT a four-step authority gradient and make it visible in the types:

1. A worker transport returns untrusted wire outcomes with exact extents, declared coverage, and receipts.
2. The JVM adapter checks schema, source identity, axis/extent membership, sidecar shape/checksum, and per-item completeness. Only then can it construct checked source observations or feature tracks.
3. Semantic outputs — action, character identity, dialogue attribution, event identity, boundaries with narrative meaning, descriptions, and local charts — enter `acquire` as `AgentProposal[A]` with typed support. A structurally checked `PropositionChart` may be the value of a proposal; structural validity does not make it an accepted narrative claim.
4. The deterministic resolver decides Accepted/Alternative/Unresolved/Rejected. Only a later compiler may incorporate accepted claims into `StoryModel` or `DocumentModel`.

The output classification should be by epistemic role, not provider family:

- scalar/vector/categorical measurement becomes a sidecar feature with observed/missing/failed coverage and derivation receipt;
- ASR text or visual description becomes proposal-bearing source text with typed support, never original transcript fact by default;
- interval, boundary, track, and identity detections become typed candidates with support and provenance;
- tracking continuity is not character identity, shot boundaries do not entail event boundaries, and a vector is structurally unable to become a proposition.

This keeps late fusion lawful: fusion may create a new derived feature or a new proposal with a dependency DAG and support union, but it cannot mutate raw observations or upgrade them to facts. Mixed-axis support requires an explicit alignment receipt; there is no numeric-time shortcut.

D6 — WORKER BOUNDARY

ACCEPT the autonomous-worker idea only with a policy-minted request and a fail-closed adapter. The portable API should describe task intent and output schemas; the transport/runtime stays JVM-only. A request must bind:

- bundle, stream, axis, and native extent identities;
- admitted source-access/rights decision and purpose;
- requested output family and schema version;
- prompt/config/preprocessing identities;
- budget, timeout/retry policy, cancellation identity, and cache key inputs.

Each returned item must be exactly one of observed, examined-with-no-candidate, abstained/unsupported, or failed, rather than disappearing from a batch. The receipt must bind bundle and byte checksums; model and exact weight revision; container/runtime; preprocessing/config; request/output schemas; attempted extent; output or sidecar digest; retry/attempt history; and whether a cache artifact was used. Large arrays remain checksum-bound sidecars, not inline graph values.

The untrusted worker does not mint cache authority, a validated feature track, `Accepted`, or an authoritative chart. The adapter verifies the wire envelope and then calls smart constructors. A cache hit must be a capability derived from a verified artifact and request key, not a public enum tag supplied by the provider; the current provider-parser self-hold is a timely warning against copying that pattern.

SMALLEST DISCRIMINATING COURT — CROSS-EDITION LATE-FUSION SUBSTITUTION

Construct bundles A and B for two editions with the same numeric PTS range and the same human-readable stream labels, but different bundle/stream/axis fingerprints and no admitted alignment. Produce:

- a valid shot interval and object feature on A;
- valid ASR text on B;
- a valid speaker track on A;
- a proposed action/character attribution whose support is on B;
- individually well-formed provider receipts and sidecars.

Then attempt to fuse them into one proposal such as `Alice performs action X at 12.0–14.0` by matching numeric time and labels. The lawful system must refuse before resolution: either the wire receipt disagrees with the declared request identity, atlas membership fails, or the evidence union lacks an explicit cross-axis alignment. The resolver must remain Unresolved/Rejected and no accepted chart/node may be emitted.

Mutation witnesses:

- replace typed axis coordinates with normalized doubles;
- omit the bundle/axis membership check;
- trust the worker-declared cache-hit tag;
- key provider agreement only by display model name;
- treat nonempty mixed support as sufficient evidence.

Any one of those mutations should make the bad fusion pass, proving that the court exercises the boundary rather than merely checking happy-path serialization. The same test should show that an explicit checked alignment can make a corresponding cross-edition projection lawful without collapsing the source identities.

Bottom line: AMEND, not BLOCK. Build the medium-neutral source/evidence substrate and its refusal laws first; migrate acquisition and features second; admit a JVM worker only after Q5 identifies exact lawful bytes and the worker cannot cross the proposal/acceptance boundary.
